column10: Direct call to the raw `hitTest` function (not the `withRotation`-wrapped version) is used to detect which text shape was clicked for double-click-to-edit. For a rotated text shape, this tests against the unrotated AABB, so a user clicking on the visually-rotated shape may fail to enter edit mode, while clicking on empty canvas (in the unrotated position) incorrectly triggers it. The registered `hitTest` at line 270 is correctly wrapped, but this internal handler at line 249 is not.

Same issue as the text plugin: the double-click-to-edit event handler calls the unwrapped `hitTest` directly. For a rotated sticky shape, the pointer-down handler tests against the unrotated AABB, so clicking the rotated shape will not reliably trigger edit mode. The registered `hitTest` at line 478 uses `withRotation`, but this handler does not.

`applyClientUpdate` returns `true` (accepted) when `doc` is `null`, without actually validating the Yjs payload. In practice `doc` is null on every Durable Object restart until `getOrCreateDoc()` is called — and `getOrCreateDoc` is never called in the WebSocket message path, only from the HTTP thumbnail/AI endpoints. So the new `applied` guard in `board-room.ts` is effectively dead code for all normal WebSocket traffic: corrupt updates still get buffered, persisted, and broadcast to every other connected client.

Concurrent callers that join while `loadPromise` is pending will `await` the same promise. If the first caller's load fails (storage error), `loadPromise` is set to `null` and the error is rethrown by the first caller — but the second caller, already suspended on `await loadPromise`, also receives the rejection and propagates it with no catch handler, causing the second request to fail with an unhandled error even though it had no fault. The same pattern exists in `partition-manager.ts`. The fix is to wrap the secondary `await loadPromise` in a try/catch and retry if `loaded` is still false.

Same concurrent-caller rejection-propagation bug as in `yjs-sync.ts`: secondary callers awaiting `loadPromise` will have the error thrown directly at them with no recovery path if the storage read fails.

`collision-utils.ts::shapeToBounds` still returns the raw unrotated bounding box, while `board-store.ts::shapeToBounds` was updated in this PR to return the expanded rotated AABB. The collision utilities (`findIntersecting`, `findContainers`, `findContained`) are now inconsistent with the spatial index: two shapes that visually overlap after rotation may be reported as non-intersecting because the collision check uses the pre-rotation rectangles. This affects frame containment detection and connector logic.

`snapAngle` can return 360 for angles just below 360 (e.g. `snapAngle(352.5, 15)` → 360). The result is not normalized to [0, 360). Since `normalizeAngle` exists in the same file, callers that pass the result directly to rotation storage or comparisons (e.g. `if (rotation === 0)` in `withRotation`/`safeRotation` paths) will treat 360 as a non-zero rotation and apply a no-op CSS transform rather than skipping it, wasting work. More importantly, stored shape data could contain `rotation: 360`, which won't match the `rotation === 0` fast-path and will run through `getRotatedAABB` unnecessarily.

A client update is broadcast to other clients *before* it's added to the list of updates to be persisted. If the server crashes after broadcasting but before `yjsSync.scheduleSave()` completes, the update will be lost, causing clients to become desynchronized. The `pushUpdate` call should happen before `broadcast`.

The JSDoc for `angleRad` says it's in radians, but the calculation `(angleDeg * Math.PI) / 180` in `getRotatedAABB` and `withRotation` suggests the original value (`angleDeg`) is in degrees. The function name `rotatePoint` doesn't specify units. The parameter should be renamed to `angleRad` and callers should consistently pass radians, or the function should be changed to accept degrees and convert internally to avoid confusion.

The style object from `s.style` is not safely accessed. If `s.style` is `null` or not an object, `(s.style as Record<string, unknown>)` will cause an error when its properties are accessed. It would be safer to define a `style` variable with a check like `typeof s.style === 'object' && s.style !== null` before accessing its properties.

The PR description states this PR adds rotation foundations (utilities, rendering, hit-test, spatial index). However, the diff also contains substantial unrelated server-side changes in `apps/server/src/rooms/yjs-sync.ts`, `apps/server/src/rooms/thumbnail-handler.ts`, `apps/server/src/rooms/partition-manager.ts`, and `apps/server/src/board-room.ts` (concurrency-safe load promise, debounced partition save, applyClientUpdate returning a boolean, etc.). These should either be split into a separate PR or added to the PR description so reviewers understand the scope.

This applies rotation only to the deprecated `ShapeLayer`, but the app registers and uses `createDomRendererPlugin()`/`DomShapeLayer` for normal rendering (for example `apps/web/src/app.tsx:64-65` and `packages/dom-renderer/src/dom-shape-layer.tsx:25-34`). As a result, the main DOM renderer still ignores `shape.rotation`, so rotated HTML shapes will not visually rotate in production.

Because `saveScheduled` stays true until after `storage.put` completes, updates that arrive after `data` is computed but before the put finishes will call `scheduleSave()`, see the flag as true, and not schedule a follow-up write. Those updates remain only in memory until a later update happens, so they can be lost if the Durable Object is evicted after this save.

This debounce has the same lost-update window as the main Yjs save: while `storage.put` is in flight, `saveScheduled` remains true, so any new update for this partition will not schedule another flush after the already-computed `data` is written. If the object is evicted before another update arrives, that partition update is never persisted.

The rotated hit tests make these GPU-backed shapes selectable as if rotated, but their GPU rendering path still ignores `rotation`: `rectGpuPrimitive`/`ellipseGpuPrimitive` are claimed by `createGpuRendererPlugin()` in the app, and `packages/gpu-renderer/src/pipelines/shape-sdf-pipeline.ts:119-122` stores only corner radius, stroke width, opacity, and shape kind. Rectangles/ellipses can therefore hit-test as rotated while still drawing unrotated.

`step` is a public input here, but `0` (or a non-finite value) produces `NaN`/`Infinity` because the function divides by it and then multiplies it back. Either validate that the snap interval is a positive finite number or define a safe fallback; otherwise callers can accidentally store an invalid rotation angle.

This test uses a 100×100 square, so a 90° rotation has the same AABB and the assertions would pass even if `withRotation` did not unrotate the point at all. Add a non-square rectangle case with a point that is inside only after applying the inverse rotation to cover the behavior being introduced.
